newsitem.title: USA: IMF offers $20 mln to back Mauritanian reforms.
newsitem.headline: IMF offers $20 mln to back Mauritanian reforms.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund said on Monday it expected growth and inflation of around five percent in the West African country of Mauritania and was backing reforms there with a $20 million loan.
An IMF statement said the loan, to be released in two tranches, was the third annual credit under a $59 million Enhanced Structural Adjustment Facility.
"The Mauritanian government has been implementing a comprehensive medium-term adjustment program, which has achieved significant results," it said.
"Savings and economic growth have rebounded, inflation has been lowered, fiscal stability has been regained and the external current account has been strengthened."
But high indebtedness meant the economy remained vulnerable to external shocks, the IMF added.

The IMF forecast GDP growth of 4.9 percent in 1997, rising to a projected 5.0 percent in 1998 and 5.3 percent in 1999. Inflation would be 5.0 percent in 1997, falling to 4.6 percent in 1998 and 4.0 percent in 1999.
